title: Grateful Dead Live at Haight Street on 1968-03-03
lineage: AUD > Uher RR > DAT > DALCardDeluxe > WAV > CDR

ai_review.summary: Rough mono audience tape captured on a Uher recorder, but the historic Haight‑Street free show shines with a scorching Viola Lee Blues and incendiary Smokestack Lightning.
ai_review.review: The recording is an old‑school mono audience capture – gritty, a bit muffled and prone to pitch wobble – yet it preserves one of the Dead’s most iconic street performances.  Musically the band is on fire: Jerry’s hypnotic lead on Viola Lee and his shredding on Smokestack Lightning are repeatedly praised, and Bobby’s extra verse on Love Light gets special mention.  Despite the technical limitations and a few missing tracks, listeners celebrate the historic atmosphere more than any sonic perfection.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 5‑star and focus on the performance’s historic excitement; recording flaws are acknowledged but not enough to outweigh the strong musical praise.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mono Uher reel‑to‑reel tape recorded with a cheap overhead mic; noticeable distortion, occasional pitch drift and drop‑outs, but overall listenable for a 1968 field recording.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, spontaneous free‑concert set typical of early ’68; the band rolls through blues‑heavy numbers with high energy, creating a street‑party vibe despite the ad‑hoc venue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is highlighted as hypnotic on Viola Lee and shredding on Smokestack Lightning.
